# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 37 MISS WINIFRED MAKES A STARTLING ANNOUNCEMENT

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Miss Winifred made her way down to the small dwelling on a sluggish afternoon, at a time when the gulf displayed the pale, faded blue characteristic of August waters, and the orange lilies standing by the gate of Nell’s garden raised their majestic blossoms to catch the liquefied gold of August sunlight. It was not that Miss Winifred paid any mind to colorful seas or thirsty lilies. She was seated in her preferred rocking chair in an uncharacteristic state of rest. She was neither sewing nor spinning. Neither did she utter a solitary disparaging remark regarding any part of humanity. To be brief, Miss Winifred’s talk lacked its customary bite on that particular day, and Hugh, who had remained at home so he could hear her talk, rather than venturing out to fish as he had planned, considered himself wronged. What had occurred to alter Miss Winifred? She failed to appear depressed or anxious. Rather, an undeniable mood of restless triumph hung about her.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0000 }

“Lorna, where is she?” was her question—spoken without much genuine concern, either.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0001 }

“In the woods behind her farm, she and Adrian were picking raspberries,” Nell replied. “Before supper—if even by that time—they will not return.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0002 }

“It appears they lack all awareness of the existence of clocks,” Hugh remarked. “That business remains a complete mystery to me. My conviction is that you women manipulated matters behind the scenes. Yet Nell, disobedient spouse that she is, refuses to enlighten me. Are you willing to, Miss Winifred?”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0003 }

“No, I will not. However,” stated Miss Winifred, assuming the manner of a person resolved to leap in and finish it, “I am going to share a different matter with you. My reason for coming today was specifically to convey it. I shall be getting married.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0004 }

Nell and Hugh kept quiet. Had Miss Winifred declared that she intended to go out to the channel and drown herself, the statement could have been believed. This, however, was unbelievable. Consequently, they waited. Naturally, Miss Winifred had committed an error.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0005 }

“Well, the pair of you appear somewhat kerflummexed,” Miss Winifred said, her eyes twinkling. With the uncomfortable instant of disclosure behind her, Miss Winifred had regained her self-possession. “Is it your belief that I lack the age and experience required for marriage?”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0006 }

“You know—it IS quite shocking,” Hugh said, attempting to collect his thoughts. “I’ve listened to you state twenty times that you wouldn’t wed the finest man on earth.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0007 }

“I will not be marrying the world’s finest man,” Miss Winifred countered. “Ambrose Kerr falls far short of being the best.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0008 }

“Will you be marrying Ambrose Kerr?” Nell cried out, regaining her ability to talk beneath this second jolt.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0009 }

“Indeed. I was able to secure him at any moment throughout the past twenty years had I raised a finger. However, do you imagine I intended to stroll into a house of worship alongside a moving haystack such as he?”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0010 }

“I am sure we are very glad—and we wish you all possible happiness,” said Nell, expressing herself, in her own opinion, quite dully and insufficiently. For such an event, she lacked preparation. Never had she pictured herself extending engagement congratulations to Miss Winifred.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0011 }

“I knew you would, thanks,” Miss Winifred said. “My friends do not know it yet, except for you.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0012 }

“Although, dear Miss Winifred, we shall be so sorry to lose you,” said Nell, starting to become slightly sentimental and sad.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0013 }

“Oh, I am not going to be lost to you,” Miss Winifred remarked without sentiment. “Do you truly imagine I could reside across the harbor alongside every one of those Crawfords, Kerrs, and MacAllisters? ‘Good Lord, save us from the pride of the MacAllisters, the conceit of the Kerrs, and the vain-glory of the Crawfords.’ Ambrose will move into my house. Hired men have completely exhausted my patience. The one I have hired for this summer, Saul Hastings, is without question the most awful of his kind. Anyone would be driven to matrimony by him. Can you imagine? Yesterday, he knocked the churn over, covering the yard in a large batch of spilled cream. Yet he felt not the slightest bit of remorse! He merely chuckled foolishly, declaring that the soil benefited from cream. Is that not typical male behavior? I informed him that using cream as fertilizer for my back yard was not my custom.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0014 }

“Well, I wish you every kind of joy as well, Miss Winifred,” Hugh said, gravely; “however,” he continued, failing to withstand the urge to poke fun at Miss Winifred, even though Nell looked at him beseechingly, “I am afraid your period of freedom has come to an end. As you are aware, Ambrose Kerr is an exceedingly resolute person.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0015 }

“A person who is capable of adhering to a course of action appeals to me,” replied Miss Winifred. “That was not the case with Amos Hollis, a former suitor of mine from years back. A more fickle individual you have never observed. On one occasion, he leapt into the body of water to end his life, yet he altered his intention subsequently and paddled back to shore. Was that not typical masculine behavior? Ambrose would have persevered in the act and perished.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0016 }

“They also inform me that his temper is somewhat quick,” Hugh pressed on.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0017 }

“He would fail to be a Kerr if he had done otherwise. That he did makes me grateful. Stirring his anger will be genuine entertainment. Furthermore, one is usually able to accomplish something with an ill-tempered man once the moment for remorse arrives. Conversely, a man who merely remains calm and exasperating offers no leverage at all.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0018 }

“Miss Winifred, you are aware that he is a Grit.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0019 }

“Yes, he IS,” Miss Winifred conceded quite mournfully. “And naturally he cannot possibly be turned into a Conservative. Yet he is a Presbyterian, at any rate. Therefore I must assume that will have to content me.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0020 }

“If he happened to be a Methodist, Miss Winifred, would you take him as your husband?”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0021 }

“No, I wouldn’t. While politics belongs strictly to this world, religion pertains to both.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0022 }

“And you could end up a ‘relict’ in the end, Miss Winifred.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0023 }

“I will not. Ambrose is going to outlive me. Longevity is a trait of the Kerrs, whereas it is absent in the Bryants.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0024 }

“When is your wedding to take place?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0025 }

“In roughly four weeks. The gown for my wedding will be made of navy blue silk. Furthermore, Nell, my dear, I would like your opinion on whether wearing a veil alongside a navy blue gown is appropriate. My desire has always been to wear a veil should I ever wed. According to Ambrose, I should wear one if it pleases me. Is that not typical of a man?”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0026 }

“If you wish to wear it, why ought you not to?” Nell asked.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0027 }

“Well, a person prefers not to stand out from everybody else,” stated Miss Winifred, who did not bear a striking resemblance to any other human being in the world. “Like I mentioned, I really would like a veil. Still, perhaps a person ought not to wear it unless the dress is white. Nell, my dear, kindly share your true opinion with me. I will follow whatever you advise.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0028 }

“Except with white dresses, veils are not typically worn,” Nell acknowledged, “yet that is just a custom; and like Mr. Kerr, I feel the same, Miss Winifred. If you desire a veil, I see no valid cause why you should be without one.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0029 }

Yet Miss Winifred, who conducted her visits wearing calico wrappers, shook her head.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0030 }

“Should it not be the correct item, I shall refrain from wearing it,” she uttered, sighing mournfully over a vanished fantasy.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0031 }

“Because you have made up your mind to get married, Miss Winifred,” Hugh stated gravely, “I will bestow upon you the superb guidelines for controlling a husband that were handed down by my grandmother to my mother upon her marriage to my father.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0032 }

“Indeed, I suppose Ambrose Kerr is within my control,” Miss Winifred stated calmly. “However, allow us to listen to your regulations.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0033 }

“Capturing him is the initial step.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0034 }

“He is trapped. Continue.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0035 }

“Give him plenty to eat is the second rule.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0036 }

“Given a sufficient amount of pie. What comes after?”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0037 }

“Pay attention to him—those are the third and fourth.”
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0038 }

“I take you at your word,” Miss Winifred declared with force.
{: #nw-v04-c37-p0039 }
